summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would authorise cost recovery levies for imported food administration where the charges fall outside the constitutional categories of customs duties and excise.
Regulations would prescribe the matters attracting charges, set amounts or calculation methods and identify who must pay, alongside existing fees for individual services.
It would work with separate customs and excise charging bills and a collection bill, with substantive operation linked to commencement of the collection arrangements.
changes: Charges would require ministerial satisfaction that they recover no more than likely Commonwealth costs.
Regulations could exclude specified matters from charging.
The framework would prohibit taxation of state-owned property.
Christmas Island and the Cocos Islands would be covered only if the imported food control legislation extends there.
summary.affected: Food importers and businesses handling imported food would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: The Imported Food Charges (Imposition-Customs) Bill 2015 was introduced as part of a four‑bill package, imposing charges only when they are considered a duty of customs, with the amounts and exemptions to be set in regulations.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: The Imported Food Charges (Imposition-Excise) Bill 2015 was introduced as part of a legislative package to impose excise charges on imported food, with the amounts and exemptions to be set in delegated legislation rather than the bill itself.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: The Imported Food Charges (Collection) Bill 2015 provides the authority to collect charges for imported food cost recovery, with regulations setting payment times, agent liability, and late fees. It includes non-payment measures such as suspending certificates and recovering debts, while allowing refunds at the Agriculture Secretary's discretion.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: The speaker defended the Auditor-General's report on imported food inspection as generally effective, disagreed with the member for Hunter's criticism, and noted three recommendations are being implemented. They also announced four Imported Food Charges bills to enable cost-recovery for food safety activities and stated the government is consulting on simpler country-of-origin food labelling, with around 8,000 responses received.
